title: Advancements in 3D spheroid imaging: Optimised cryosectioning and immunostaining techniques
author: Charlet-Faure, Thulesen, et al.
materials: Sodium Citrate Buffer (10 mM Sodium Citrate, 0.05% Tween 20, pH 6.0)
Tissue freezing medium, PolyFreeze, Sigma-Aldrich® (Cat. nr. SHH0025, Merck)
Standard Tissue-Tek® Cryomolds®, 20 × 25 mm, 5 mm height (Sakura® Finetek, Cat. No.4557)

steps.title: Prepare HepG2/C3A spheroids
steps.instruction: Generate 21‑day‑old HepG2/C3A spheroids (≈800–900 µm diameter) following the published method of reference [2].

steps.title: Antigen retrieval of fixed spheroids
steps.instruction: Perform heat‑mediated antigen retrieval on fixed spheroids using the specified retrieval solution and sucrose wash.

substeps.instruction: Immerse fixed spheroids in 200 µL retrieval solution and incubate at 4 °C for ≥8 h (or overnight).
Pre‑heat a fresh 200 µL portion of retrieval solution to 92–95 °C.
Replace the cold solution with 1 mL of the pre‑heated solution and incubate at 92–95 °C for 10 min.
Remove the retrieval solution.
Add 1 mL of 30 % sucrose solution (kept at 4 °C).
Incubate at 4 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Embed spheroids in cryomould
steps.instruction: Place spheroids in a freezing medium block within a disposable cryomould, eliminate air bubbles, and freeze.

substeps.instruction: Fold and compress a piece of aluminium foil to create a 3 × 35 mm thin band.
Add a 1–2 mm layer of freezing medium to the bottom of the disposable cryomould.
Place the aluminium band diagonally in the mould to split it into two triangles.
Place spheroids on top of the freezing medium, ensuring they do not touch each other or the mould walls.
Remove any liquid that adheres to the spheroids.
Cover spheroids with a small amount of freezing medium (do not overfill).
Place an empty mould on top and apply gentle pressure to remove air bubbles and create a uniform block.
Invert the specimen so spheroids detach from the mould bottom and migrate toward the centre of the freezing medium.
Freeze the specimen by placing it on dry ice as soon as spheroids are free of the mould walls.
Wait 5–10 min for the freezing medium to solidify.
Store the frozen tissue blocks at –80 °C.

steps.title: Cryosection embedded spheroids
steps.instruction: Section the frozen blocks in a cryostat, collect slices on cold slides, and store them frozen.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the cryotome at least 1 h before use; set Cryobar to –50 °C, Chamber to –24 °C, and Specimen to –13 °C.
Prepare dry ice for storage of samples and the slide box.
Place the frozen specimen in the cryotome chamber to prevent thawing.
Remove the sample from the plastic mould and split the freezing‑medium square into two triangles at the aluminium‑foil line.
Apply a thin layer of freezing medium onto the cryocassette and attach the sample with the triangle base facing downwards.
Place the cryocassette onto the cryobar and allow the freezing medium to solidify.
Secure the cryocassette in the quick‑release clamp on the specimen head.
Adjust the specimen‑to‑blade distance so the sample is close to the knife.
Set the knife to obtain sections 5–30 µm thick (recommended for fluorescence).
Cut the block until a spheroid structure appears.
Collect each desired slice with a pre‑cooled tweezer and place it on a cold glass slide.
Press gently on the slide bottom with a fingertip to promote adhesion and eliminate air bubbles.
Keep the glass slides and tweezer frozen (store them in the cryostat or on the cryobar) while cutting.
Inspect slices with a light microscope to confirm presence of spheroid structures.
Store the collected slides at –80 °C.

steps.title: Immunostain cryosections for α‑SMA
steps.instruction: Stain the cryosectioned spheroids for α‑smooth muscle actin using the published immunostaining protocol and Alexa Fluor® 488 anti‑α‑SMA antibody (ab267536).

description: The methods presented in this protocol were tested using 21-day-old HepG2/C3A spheroids stained for alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) (Uniprot Accession Number P62736). 21-day-old HepG2/C3A spheroids are large, approximately 800 to 1000 µm pseudo tissue structures with a viable rim and necrotic core [3,8]. Such spheroids are dense and difficult to analyse using fluorescent light microscopy without sectioning. At the same time, spheroids are fragile and difficult to cut into thin sections without distorting their shape or damaging the internal structures. The presented protocol was compared to a standard cryosectioning and immunostaining protocol [2] and validated using two antigen retrieval conditions with 4 and 10 min heat extraction protocols. The results demonstrate a significant increase in α-SMA staining intensity, with the highest intensity observed after a 10 min heat extraction, Fig. 2, while maintaining spheroid integrity without visible damage. Alterations in tissue embedding and cryosectioning protocols were validated, as previous methods resulted in distorted and broken spheroids, Fig. 3A and B. In contrast, the method outlined in this study improved the quality of cryosections with fewer damaged spheroids and better preservation of their shapes, Fig. 3C and D. As a result of the improved spheroid integrity, thinner sections (10 µm) were obtained, reducing the number of overlapping cell layers, and resulting in clearer and more detailed images, particularly at higher magnifications, Fig. 4.Fig. 2Preparation of embedded specimen.
